relevance_note: The paper reports one in-scope patient with SSADH deficiency and individual-level detail ('a 15-month-old girl with SSADH deficiency presenting with developmental delay, language deficits, and acute-onset right hemiparesis'), plus relatives described in relation to her and two previously reported probands with the same genotype.
method_note: Read the full Markdown (no supplementary material present) and transcribed everything by hand; no script was used. Labels: the paper's own labels for its patient and for the two literature patients are role words ('Proband in our report', 'Proband from Pakistan origin[1]', 'Proband from Palestinian-Lebanese origin[1]'), which the instructions say are not labels, so I used rule 5 ('patient') for the single patient of the case report and the table-column rule for the two literature patients ('Table 1 column 2', 'Table 1 column 3'); the column headers are named here. Relatives: the paper names 'her mother' (with paralytic poliomyelitis) and separately 'her parents' as carriers of the variant, so I recorded 'mother of patient' (sex stated) and 'parent of patient' for the second, unstated parent, rather than two generic parent labels; the unaffected sibling is 'sibling of patient'. Inheritance for the proband is recorded as 'inherited unspecified parent' although the paper states that both parents are heterozygous carriers, because no single-parent option fits a homozygous variant; the parents' and sibling's variant-identity fields are filled from the statement that they carry 'the same variant' whose description is printed once (transcript and genomic coordinates were not propagated to them). Stacked cells: Table 1 is a table with patients as columns; several cells hold several values printed on separate lines that the conversion ran together without ' / ' (for example '| Hypotonia | Yes | Normal tone at presentation Hypotonia at follow-up | Yes |' and '| Natural course | Resolution of hemiparesis Hypotonia persists Developmental gains are observed on treatment |'), so no positional assignment was made: each such value belongs to the patient of its own column, and no value was moved between columns. 'Age at presentation' in Table 1 was recorded as age at onset. Table 1 'Extrapyramidal symptoms: No' was recorded as a feature for the two people concerned but was not mapped onto the narrower checklist items (dystonia, exertional dyskinesia, hemiballismus), which are left 'not reported'; 'Reflexes: Normal' for the Pakistan-origin proband was recorded as excluding 'abnormal deep tendon reflexes'. 'Developmental delay' was recorded as a feature and 'intellectual disability' left 'not reported'; 'stranger anxiety' is listed among this child's developmental milestones and was not recorded as anxiety, and 'fidgetiness'/'fleeting eye contact' were not mapped to attention problems/ADHD. The in silico prediction ('predicted to be pathogenic by various in silico prediction analysis tools') is not a functional assay and was not recorded as functional evidence. The alternative nomenclature discussed for the same variant (c.1343 + 1delG and c.1343 + 3A>T) was not entered as separate variant rows because the authors argue it is the same 'indel' event. publications.n_patients_reported = 1 (one patient with a variant described first-hand); the two Table 1 probands are recorded as separate individuals with source_reference_in_review '[1]', and cites_prior_report_of_same_patients = true because the paper states that those two cases were reported previously. No internal contradictions were found.
